title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
layout_note: Two rounded panels in one row: the wider left panel is the prior pipeline, the narrower right panel the proposed one; the shorter pipeline is visibly a shorter panel.
grouping: Each approach is a rounded panel with a tinted background (muted pink for the prior pipeline, pale teal for the proposed one) and a bold sans title in its top-left corner. No inner boxes: the steps float on the panel tint.
shapes_depth: No boxes at all. Preference data is two outline speech-bubble icons with lines of text, joined by a 'greater than' sign, with a small trophy icon on the preferred one and a short quoted example prompt above; each model is a faint node-and-edge network glyph with its name written large over it ('reward model', 'LM policy', 'final LM'). Two curved arrows form the loop between reward model and policy, each with a lower-case label. Thick black straight arrows; rounded sans text throughout.
proposed_highlight: The objective of each step is written under its arrow in bold colour: 'maximum likelihood' in the same teal in both panels, 'reinforcement learning' in red under the loop that only the prior pipeline has. The proposed panel takes the teal tint, so its whole panel matches the shared, simpler objective.
lesson: Name the training objective under each arrow in bold coloured words, the same colour for a step both pipelines share and a contrasting colour for the step only the baseline needs, so the reader sees what was removed without a legend.
notes: The whole figure is one embedded raster in the PDF (a vector-style diagram exported as an image); kb measure left photo_share null and measured the palette over the whole crop. Venue and year from the PDF footer (NeurIPS 2023).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: aligning language models to human preferences
taxonomy.note: architecture other: pipeline comparison, no network architecture drawn

core.what: prior method and ours as two tinted panels side by side, a wide pink RLHF panel then a narrower teal DPO panel, each starting from the same drawn preference data, so the shorter pipeline is visibly the shorter panel

relations.form: two rounded tinted panels on one row, RLHF left and DPO (ours) right and last, with the preference-data drawing repeated identically at the left of each
within each panel one straight black arrow runs left to right from preference data to the model it trains (reward model in RLHF, final LM in DPO)
in RLHF two curved arrows between reward model and LM policy form a loop labelled 'label rewards' and 'sample completions'
preference data drawn as two speech bubbles, y_w with a trophy and y_l, joined by a '>' sign under a quoted prompt

channels.colour: panel tint = method (pink RLHF, teal DPO); objective names are coloured by type, teal 'maximum likelihood' in both panels and red 'reinforcement learning' only in RLHF; teal therefore carries both 'DPO' (panel tint) and 'maximum-likelihood objective' (label), which here deliberately reinforce each other
channels.shape: speech bubble = completion, faint node-edge network glyph = model
channels.line: straight arrow = training/data flow, curved arrows = the RL loop
channels.frame: one tinted rounded panel = one method

quality.strengths: The comparison is carried by geometry: identical inputs, ours last, and the DPO panel is physically shorter because it has one step instead of a loop; the data are drawn as data (a quoted prompt and two ranked completion bubbles with a trophy); each arrow carries its objective by name instead of a loss box.
quality.weaknesses: The network glyphs are so faint they read as background texture behind the model names; teal doubles as the DPO panel tint and the maximum-likelihood label colour, so the reader may take the RLHF reward-model step as 'DPO-like'; the RL loop's two arcs are not tied to a policy-update arrow.

insights.structure: Two rounded tinted panels side by side: a wide pink 'RLHF' panel (preference data -> reward model <-> LM policy) and a narrower teal 'DPO' panel (preference data -> final LM), so the shorter pipeline is visibly the shorter panel.
insights.data: Preference data is two speech-bubble icons (y_w with a trophy, y_l) joined by a greater-than sign under a quoted prompt 'write me a poem about the history of jazz'; models are faint node-and-edge network glyphs with their names written large over them.
insights.emphasis: Each step's objective is written below its arrow in bold colour: 'maximum likelihood' in the same teal in both panels and 'reinforcement learning' in red only in the RLHF panel, and the DPO panel takes the teal tint.
insights.flow: Left to right within each panel with thick black straight arrows; in RLHF two curved arrows form a loop labelled 'label rewards' and 'sample completions'.
insights.avoid: The network glyphs are so faint they read as background texture, so the models are recognised only by their text labels.

arrangement.units: two rounded tinted panels, one per method, bold title in the top-left corner, no inner boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: speech-bubble icons for the preferred and dispreferred completions under a quoted example prompt
arrangement.losses_at: objective names in bold colour under each arrow
arrangement.shared: the same preference-data drawing repeated at the left of both panels; teal 'maximum likelihood' repeated
